sections.h2: What are my choices when I want to sell a house in Kent?
sections.html:
A Kent owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a purchase offer from a buyer who does not need a mortgage. Each path trades time, effort and price differently, so line them up against your own deadline before you decide.

  • Listing with an agent: Expect to stage, clean and repair, then wait through showings and a buyer's inspection and loan approval.
  • Selling on your own: You keep control of price and terms and take on the marketing, the contract and the closing paperwork yourself.
  • Selling to a cash buyer: The sale moves without lender underwriting. Ask for the net amount you would receive at closing and compare it with the other two routes.

A building with tenants raises extra questions, covered below, because Kent runs its own rental inspection program.

sections.h2: How is Kent laid out, and where does flooding come up?
sections.html:
Kent is divided into three sections: West Hill, along Interstate 5; the Valley, mostly industrial and commercial with some medium-density housing and parkland along the Green River; and East Hill, which is largely residential with retail. Downtown Kent sits on the east side of the valley, about 16 miles from downtown Seattle and downtown Bellevue. Renton, Covington, Auburn, Federal Way, Des Moines, SeaTac and Tukwila all touch the city. The city covers 34.167 square miles, and Lake Meridian on East Hill is its largest lake, with Clark Lake and Lake Fenwick surrounded by city parks.

The Green River matters to anyone selling in the Valley. Wikipedia notes that flooding from the Green and White rivers was a constant problem in the early 1900s, and that the river kept causing trouble until Howard A. Hanson Dam went up at Eagle Gorge in 1962. The City of Kent maintains a Floodplains page with flood resources and FEMA elevation certificates, plus a Green River flooding information page. If your house is near the river, ask the city for the elevation certificate and floodplain status before a buyer asks.

sections.h2: What shaped Kent's economy and population?
sections.html:
Kent was incorporated on May 28, 1890, the second city in King County after Seattle. Its early money came from hops, and the town took its name in 1889 from the English hop county; later came dairy, then a stretch as the lettuce capital of the world. After World War II the city grew quickly, twelvefold between 1953 and 1960, and Boeing began building in Kent in 1965.

Today the Valley is a warehouse and manufacturing district. Wikipedia says manufacturing and distribution in Kent and the surrounding area ranks fourth among markets in the United States. Blue Origin and Stoke Space have their headquarters here, and Amazon, Boeing, Whirlpool and General Electric run large facilities. On July 1, 2010 the city annexed the Panther Lake area, adding about 5 square miles and 24,000 residents.

sections.h2: Does Kent regulate rental housing, and does that touch my sale?
sections.html:
Yes, for buildings with two or more units. The City Council passed an ordinance in 2018 requiring periodic health and safety inspections by a qualified inspector for apartments, townhomes, fourplexes, triplexes and duplexes inside city limits. A standalone house is not on that list. If you own a duplex or a small building and plan to sell, the program shapes what a buyer will ask about.

  • Registration: Covered rentals are registered online every year, with a deadline of November 1. The 2026 date has passed, and the next is November 1, 2027.
  • Inspection cycle: Each property is inspected once every three years. North East Hill, north of James Street, is on the 2026 cycle; West Hill and the Valley, west of Highway 167, are due in 2027; South East Hill, south of James Street, in 2028.
  • Penalties: Owners whose units fail must make repairs and pass reinspection before renewing the multi-family business license. Failure can bring penalty fees and revocation of the license.

For license questions, the city lists 253-856-5200. Ask the city which cycle year your address falls in before you set a closing date, and keep the latest inspection paperwork with your sale file.

sections.h2: What do I file and pay at closing on a Kent sale?
sections.html:
The big item is the state real estate excise tax. According to the Department of Revenue, the seller usually pays it, and if the seller does not, the buyer is responsible. State tax is 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 of the price and 1.28 percent on the next slice up to $1,525,000, with a local rate added. A Kent sale at the $587,800 median home value would carry about $6,579 in state tax, made up of $5,775 and about $804.

A transfer by deed needs an excise tax affidavit, the deed and payment. The department warns that mailing the affidavit and deed to the Department of Revenue by mistake can delay the filing with the county and lead to penalties and interest. Take them to the county treasurer where the property sits, which for Kent is King County, or let your escrow officer handle the filing. Payment is due on the date of sale, and penalty and interest apply if it is not paid within one month.

sections.h2: Which permits does Kent ask about on a house sale?
sections.html:
Kent's Permit Center takes electronic applications by appointment and issues residential permits for additions and alterations, plumbing, re-roofing and mechanical work. The city publishes separate short forms for a residential plumbing permit, which covers replacing fixtures and hot water tanks, for a re-roof, and for mechanical equipment including gas piping. If a previous owner swapped a water heater or replaced a roof, ask the Permit Center whether a permit was pulled, and check the Permit Logs page for issued permits.

Code Enforcement is the city office tasked with keeping Kent safe and beautiful, so ask it whether any case is open on your property before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and schools affect Kent buyers?
sections.html:
State Route 167 runs north to Renton and south to Puyallup, and the city also includes parts of Interstate 5 and State Route 18, with State Route 516 crossing east to west. Kent Station is the hub for Sounder commuter trains to Seattle and Tacoma, plus King County Metro and Sound Transit Express buses, and RapidRide A runs along SR 99 in west Kent. The I Line is scheduled to connect downtown Kent with Renton and Auburn in 2027. Average travel time to work is 30.4 minutes.

The Kent School District covers most of the city, with four high schools, seven middle schools, 28 elementary schools and two academies. Parts of Kent fall in Federal Way Public Schools, Tahoma, Highline or the Renton School District, so confirm the district for your address when you write a listing or describe the house to a buyer.

faqs.q: Does Kent's rental inspection program cover a single-family house?
faqs.a: No. The program's list is apartments, townhomes, fourplexes, triplexes and duplexes, each with two or more units. Owners of those buildings register every year by November 1 and have an inspection once every three years.

faqs.q: Where do I file the excise tax affidavit for a Kent sale?
faqs.a: With the county treasurer in the county where the property is located, which is King County for Kent. The Department of Revenue says to submit the affidavit, the deed and the payment there, and warns that sending them to the department by mistake can cause delays.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Kent address?
faqs.a: Most of Kent is in the Kent School District. Portions are in Federal Way Public Schools, the Tahoma School District, Highline Public Schools or the Renton School District, with far east Kent zoned to Tahoma, so check the district for your specific address.

faqs.q: How far is Kent from Seattle?
faqs.a: Downtown Kent is about 16 miles from downtown Seattle and downtown Bellevue. State Route 167 and Interstate 5 are the main roads, and Sounder trains run from Kent Station to downtown Seattle during peak weekday hours.

faqs.q: Is flood risk a concern for Kent houses?
faqs.a: It can be in the Green River Valley. Howard A. Hanson Dam went up in 1962 after decades of flooding, and the city keeps a Floodplains page with FEMA elevation certificates. Ask the city about floodplain status for your parcel.
